newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ says Iran recalls ambassador, trade ban in doubt.
newsitem.headline: NZ says Iran recalls ambassador, trade ban in doubt.

text.p: New Zealand said on Monday that Iran was recalling its ambassador to Wellington in the latest move in an international diplomatic row.
But a senior minister said reports that Iran had imposed a trade ban on New Zealand might have been the result of a misunderstanding, and had not yet been officially confirmed.
"Their ambassador is...being recalled," International Trade Minister Lockwood Smith told a news conference.

On Friday, New Zealand recalled its ambassador to Iran for consultations as part of a coordinated international response to a German court ruling that Tehran had ordered four political killings in 1992.
Smith said Wellington had still not received any confirmation of a report on Saturday by Iran's official news agency IRNA that Iran had banned trade with New Zealand.
"There has been no official confirmation from Iran...there could have been some misunderstanding of this," he said.
The minister said it was possible that an initial report about New Zealand's move to withdraw its ambassador on Friday had suggested Wellington wanted to curb trade ties with Iran.
"New Zealand has never linked trade to these (political) issues," he said, emphasising that no such action was planned.
Smith said the return of Iran's envoy to Tehran could help clear up any confusion over the trade issue.
"He knows New Zealand is not planning any trade embargoes," he said.
Wellington expects its ambassador, Daniel Richards, to return to Iran by end of this week.
Smith said he also feared the initial message that Richards was being withdrawn only temporarily might not have been made clearly enough, adding to the confusion.
The minister said New Zealand's trade in primary exports with Iran, which industry sources estimate was worth about NZ$170 million ($119 million) last year, was not the main issue at stake.
Asked about the possible financial impact of a trade dispute, Smith said, "That's not the point... We have always had good relations with Iran and we want to get them back on a good footing."
